sources.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits
sources.model: Shor-family factoring construction with explicit error-correction and layout assumptions
sources.boundary: Resource estimate under stated assumptions; not evidence that such a machine currently exists or has executed the attack.

sources.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits
sources.author: Craig Gidney
sources.model: Updated Shor-family RSA-2048 resource estimate under large-scale error-corrected superconducting assumptions
sources.boundary: Preprint estimate, not a demonstrated RSA-2048 attack and not evidence of an existing operational CRQC.

sources.comparison_rule: Optical modes, squeezed states, detected photons, logical qubits, and physical error-corrected qubits are different resource measures and must not be numerically substituted for one another without an explicit architecture/algorithm mapping.

required_discriminator_for_promotion: A demonstrated factoring or discrete-log attack at cryptographically relevant key size, or
an independently reproducible mapping from the operational machine architecture to the required fault-tolerant logical circuit with measured error budget and runtime, plus
evidence that the mapped machine actually exists and operates at the required scale.
